metadata.title: Are life goals invariant across different sociocultural and economic conditions? A study on a representative sample of adolescents

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The study uses IEA ICCS 2016 microdata for Italian eighth graders (students nested within classes) and applies the ICCS complex survey design in Mplus using the “Type = complex” approach. The analysis specifies a sampling weight variable (TOTWGTS) and clusters observations at the class level (CODCL) to account for stratification and non-independence. This weighting/complex-design handling is used for the confirmatory bifactor CFA, measurement invariance testing, and latent mean difference comparisons. The paper does not report replicate-weight methods (e.g., BRR/jackknife), so uncertainty is handled via the complex-design standard errors rather than explicit replicate variance estimation.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: Plausible Values are not applicable because the dependent variables are life-aspiration indices derived from questionnaire items and modeled via confirmatory bifactor CFA/measurement invariance, rather than cognitive achievement scores that ICCS/PISA typically represent with PVs. The paper instead uses full information maximum likelihood (FIML) for missing questionnaire responses in Mplus, which is appropriate for latent variable modeling and does not involve PV generation/combining.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Analytic sample consists of 3460 Italian eighth-grade students participating in ICCS 2016. Sampling followed the IEA design: 170 schools from the population of Italian lower secondary schools, with one randomly selected eighth-grade class per school. The paper does not describe additional task-level exclusions beyond the ICCS questionnaire administration; missing responses were handled with Mplus FIML for a very small proportion of missing data (0.2% to 2.5%). Analyses were conducted for the full Italian sample, with additional measurement-invariance robustness checks using a matched native subsample of size n=329 to balance native vs immigrant group sizes.

main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using ICCS 2016 the study leveraged Socioeconomic status (SES), Immigrant background (native vs immigrant), Gender (girls vs boys) to predict Primary study outcome (heuristic migration), finding that This study analyzes ICCS 2016 questionnaire data for 3460 Italian eighth-grade students to test whether the Goal Content Theory bifactor structure of life aspirations is invariant across socioeconomic status, immigrant background, and gender. Using Mplus 8.7 with the “Type = complex” approach, the authors fit a bifactor CFA model (intrinsic/extrinsic general orientations plus six specific aspirations) and then conduct multi-group measurement invariance tests (configural, metric, scalar) with strict cutoffs (e.g., ΔCFI < 0.010; ΔRMSEA < 0.015; ΔSRMR < 0.030). Latent mean difference tests show that low-SES adolescents report lower intrinsic general orientation and higher wealth and appearance aspirations, while immigrant adolescents score higher on extrinsic general orientation; gender differences include higher intrinsic orientation for females and higher extrinsic orientation for males, plus gender-specific patterns for appearance and wealth. The paper reports standardized mean differences (e.g., extrinsic general orientation: natives vs immigrants d=0.153; females vs males d=0.530***; intrinsic general orientation: females vs males d=-0.460*), but it is cross-sectional, so causal claims are not supported. This indicates that these patterns have implications for educational policy and instructional practice, though cross-sectional ILSA designs cannot establish causality.

data.null_fields_interpretation: This is not an empirical machine-learning prediction/classification paper. The study uses confirmatory factor analysis, measurement invariance testing, and latent mean difference tests in a bifactor measurement framework (Mplus), rather than training ML models with predictive performance metrics. Therefore, ml_techniques and main_findings are intentionally left empty, and the extracted “findings” are summarized narratively in outcome_summary.
